title: Dolpo trekking guide: Phoksundo, Tarap and Shey
meta_description: Dolpo trekking guide: Lower vs Upper Dolpo, permits, Juphal flights, routes from 8 to 24 nights, seasons, camping and what it really costs.
summary: Dolpo is Nepal's most remote trekking region, reached by flights from Nepalgunj to Juphal. Lower Dolpo, with Phoksundo Lake and the Tarap valley, needs a modest restricted-area permit; Upper Dolpo, with Shey Gompa and Saldang, costs USD 500 for 10 days. Both need a licensed guide, and most routes need camping.

sections.heading: Where Dolpo is
paras: Dolpo, written Dolpa for the district, lies in Karnali Province in western Nepal, behind the Dhaulagiri and Kanjiroba ranges and west of Mustang. Its northern valleys sit on the edge of the Tibetan plateau, in a rain shadow so deep that barley fields and villages survive above 4,000 m. Most of the region falls within Shey Phoksundo National Park, created in 1984 and, at about 3,555 square kilometres, the largest national park in Nepal.

Few places in Nepal are as hard to reach. There is no road into the upper valleys, mobile signal is patchy or absent, and supplies still arrive by mule, yak or on people's backs. That remoteness is exactly why trekkers come: Dolpo gives you a way of life, landscapes and silence that are now rare in the Himalaya.

sections.heading: Lower Dolpo and Upper Dolpo
paras: For permits, Dolpo is split in two. Lower Dolpo covers the southern valleys, including Dunai, Phoksundo Lake, Ringmo and the Tarap valley with Dho Tarap. Upper Dolpo covers the north beyond Phoksundo: Shey Gompa, the Nangkhong valley with Saldang and Namgung, and the villages near the Tibetan border. Upper Dolpo is far more expensive to enter and far less visited.

Both are restricted areas. Permits are issued only through registered agencies to groups of at least two foreigners with a licensed guide. On top of the restricted-area permit you pay the national park entry fee. The figures below are as we understand them; check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Getting there
paras: Almost every Dolpo trek begins with two flights. The first is from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, a hot town in the Terai near the Indian border, about an hour by air. Most trekkers spend a night there. The second is a morning flight in a small plane from Nepalgunj to Juphal, about 40 minutes, landing on a short hillside airstrip at about 2,475 m. From Juphal it is a three-hour walk to Dunai, the district headquarters.

Juphal flights depend on clear weather in the hills and are often delayed, sometimes for days in cloudy periods. Build two spare days into your plans for the return. Rough roads are slowly being extended toward Dunai from the south, but for trekkers the flight remains the practical way in.

sections.heading: Routes, from short to very long
paras: Dolpo treks range from a week to a month. Times below are from Kathmandu and back, including the flights and a buffer. Every route can be adapted, but the passes set the limits: Numa La, Baga La, Kang La, Saldang La and Jeng La are all above 5,000 m and need settled weather.
list: Phoksundo Lake, 8 to 10 nights: Juphal, Dunai, Chhepka and Ringmo, with a rest day at the lake. Lodges on most nights; the easiest Dolpo trek
Lower Dolpo circuit, 13 to 16 nights: up the Tarap gorge to Dho Tarap, over Numa La and Baga La to Phoksundo, then out. Camping needed for the high section
Upper Dolpo traverse, 22 to 26 nights: Phoksundo, Kang La to Shey Gompa, Saldang, Jeng La to the Tarap valley and down the Tarap gorge. Full camping expedition
Dolpo to Mustang, around four weeks: from Upper Dolpo east via Charka to Upper Mustang and Jomsom. Both restricted permits; for very experienced trekkers only

sections.heading: Phoksundo Lake in brief
paras: Phoksundo is the reason most people first come to Dolpo. The lake lies at about 3,610 m, held back by an ancient landslide dam, and has been measured at about 145 m deep, the deepest lake in Nepal. Its colour shifts through the day from deep blue to turquoise, depending on the light and the season. At its southern end, the stone village of Ringmo and its chortens stand on the old dam, and a short walk away a Bon monastery sits on the shore.

Below the lake, the outflow drops over a tall waterfall into the gorge of the Phoksundo Khola, which you pass on the way up from Chhepka. The trail along the west shore, cut into the cliff above the water, is the route north toward Shey and Upper Dolpo. Local people regard the lake as sacred, so visitors should not swim, fish or wash in it.

sections.heading: When to go
paras: The trekking season in Dolpo is shorter than in most of Nepal. May and June, and September and October, are the best months. Because Dolpo lies in the rain shadow, the upper valleys stay fairly dry in July and August, and some groups trek then, but monsoon cloud in the lower hills disrupts Juphal flights and makes the trails below Dunai muddy and prone to landslides.

From November, snow begins to close the high passes, and by December many people in the upper villages move to lower ground for the winter. Phoksundo itself can be visited in early November and in April, but expect frozen mornings and some closed lodges. Winter treks are possible only as specialised expeditions.

sections.heading: The people of Dolpo
paras: The Dolpo-pa, the people of Dolpo, speak a Tibetan dialect and follow Tibetan Buddhism or Bon, the pre-Buddhist religion of Tibet, which survives here more strongly than almost anywhere. Ringmo by Phoksundo Lake and parts of the Tarap valley have Bon monasteries; you can tell Bon chortens and prayer walls because followers walk around them anticlockwise. Shey Gompa and the monasteries of Saldang and Namgung are Buddhist.

Most Dolpo-pa families farm barley, buckwheat and potatoes and keep yaks, sheep and goats. Trade with Tibet, once based on exchanging salt for grain, still matters. In late spring many families also go to the high pastures to collect yarsagumba, the caterpillar fungus prized in Chinese medicine, which has become one of the region's main sources of cash. If you trek in May or June, you may find villages half-empty for this reason.

Two works made Dolpo known abroad: Peter Matthiessen's book The Snow Leopard, about his 1973 journey to Shey Gompa with the biologist George Schaller, and Eric Valli's film Himalaya, released in some countries as Caravan, shot among Dolpo's salt caravans in the late 1990s with local people in the lead roles.

sections.heading: Camping, cost and safety
paras: Apart from the Phoksundo route, Dolpo is a camping region. Your agency supplies a guide, cook, kitchen crew, tents and mules or porters. This, together with the flights and permits, makes Dolpo more expensive than lodge treks. As a guide, a 13-night Lower Dolpo circuit costs from about USD 3,400 per person and a 24-night Upper Dolpo traverse from about USD 7,500, both for two people sharing and including permits.

Rescue is slow. Helicopter evacuation is possible in good weather but can take hours or longer, so your insurance must cover high-altitude trekking and evacuation. Choose an agency whose guides carry a satellite device, plan proper acclimatisation days, and be prepared to turn back from a pass if the weather or your body says so.
list: A sleeping bag rated to −15 °C or colder for Upper Dolpo
Warm down jacket, gloves and hat, even in summer
Water treatment: tablets or a filter, since there are few shops
Cash in Nepali rupees, as there are no ATMs beyond Nepalgunj
A power bank or solar charger

faqs.a: For experienced trekkers who value remoteness and culture over comfort, yes. Dolpo offers Nepal's deepest lake at Phoksundo, high passes, Bon and Buddhist monasteries and villages that see few visitors. It is harder, costlier and less comfortable than Everest or Annapurna treks, and flights are unreliable, so it suits people with time and patience.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Lower and Upper Dolpo?
faqs.a: Lower Dolpo is the southern part, with Phoksundo Lake, Ringmo and the Tarap valley; its permit costs about USD 20 per week. Upper Dolpo is the northern part beyond Phoksundo, with Shey Gompa and Saldang; its permit costs USD 500 for 10 days. Upper Dolpo is more remote, higher and needs a longer camping trek. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I get to Dolpo?
faqs.a: Fly from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, about one hour, and stay overnight. The next morning, fly from Nepalgunj to Juphal, about 40 minutes, then walk three hours to Dunai. There is no road into the upper valleys. Allow two spare days at the end of the trek for flight delays at Juphal.

faqs.q: Can I trek in Dolpo without a guide?
faqs.a: No. Both Lower and Upper Dolpo are restricted areas, and permits are issued only to groups of at least two foreigners with a licensed guide through a registered agency. National park rules introduced in 2023 also require licensed guides. In practice, you need a crew for camping anyway. Check current status before you travel.

Only on some routes. The Phoksundo trek from Juphal to Ringmo has simple lodges in most villages. Dunai, Dho Tarap and Juphal also have lodges. The high routes over Numa La, Baga La and into Upper Dolpo have none, so you need tents, a cook and supplies.

faqs.q: What is the best month to trek Dolpo?
faqs.a: May, June, September and October are best, when the passes are usually open and the weather settled. July and August are drier in Dolpo than in most of Nepal, but Juphal flights are disrupted more often. From November, snow closes the high passes and many villagers move to lower ground.

faqs.q: How hard is the Phoksundo Lake trek?
faqs.a: The short trek to Phoksundo is moderate. You walk five to seven hours a day on clear trails, and the highest night is at Ringmo, about 3,640 m. There are no high passes. It is a good introduction to Dolpo for anyone who has done a teahouse trek before, and needs only a lower-cost permit.

Bon is a religious tradition of Tibet that existed before Buddhism arrived and has since absorbed many Buddhist forms. It survives in parts of Dolpo, including Ringmo by Phoksundo Lake and the Tarap valley. Bon followers walk around chortens and turn prayer wheels anticlockwise, the opposite of Buddhists. Respect monastery rules and ask before photographing.

faqs.q: Can I see snow leopards in Dolpo?
faqs.a: Snow leopards live in Shey Phoksundo National Park, but sightings are rare. They are shy, well camouflaged and active at dawn and dusk. Blue sheep, their main prey, are common and easy to see. Specialised winter wildlife expeditions improve the odds, but they are cold, long and demanding.
